sovereign_country.strategic_role: 亚太高客单价数字内容、游戏出海与本土电商合规

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (statute-based, centralized Supreme Court registry and National Tax Service registration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, as amended by the 2006 Protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Korean AML/CFT and UBO regime is governed by the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10452, Sept. 27, 2011, as amended, and its Enforcement Decree), the Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy Act (Act No. 5493, Jan. 21, 1998, as amended), the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, Jan. 27, 1962, as amended) including shareholder-register and corporate registration rules, the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment, and Financial Services Commission/KoFIU guidance. Korea does not operate a publicly searchable central UBO register; financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses must identify and report beneficial ownership to KoFIU on a government-only access basis.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (certified corporate registration extract from the Supreme Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, local district court registry office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain certified extract, then have the signature/seal of the registry official notarized by a Korean notary public. For recipient states party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-party states, obtain consular legalization from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then from the destination state's embassy/consulate in Korea. The two authentication tracks are parallel and mutually exclusive; an Apostille is never chained to consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean equivalent: certified corporate registration extract showing no dissolution/winding-up entry plus National Tax Service certificate of no tax arrears)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea local district court registry office and National Tax Service local tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the registry extract and the tax clearance certificate separately; notarize each original/certified copy with a Korean notary public; for Hague Apostille member states obtain Apostille certificates from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; for non-member states obtain consular legalization through MOFA and the destination embassy/consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, mutually exclusive paths and must not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation filings and financing/lease signings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Promoters and incorporating shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa to be formed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Prepare a bilingual English/Korean board resolution and power of attorney, have each signatory's identity authenticated by a Korean notary public, and cover the notarized instrument with either an Apostille (Hague member states) or consular legalization by MOFA and the destination consulate (non-member states). Never use both authentication paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Promoters and the notary public executing the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use the notarially executed Articles of Incorporation registered with the court; for external production obtain a certified copy, notarize it, and then apply for an Apostille with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination is an Apostille state, or consular legalization through MOFA and the receiving embassy/consulate if the destination is a non-Apostille state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean relationship bank (e.g., Shinhan Bank, KEB Hana Bank, Woori Bank, or KB Kookmin Bank) after account opening proof
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank issue on corporate letterhead with bank officer's authenticating signature and corporate seal; have the officer's capacity notarized, then obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille member states or consular legalization for non-member states via MOFA and the destination consulate/embassy. The letter may also be sent through the SWIFT bank channel where the receiving registry accepts such direct verification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, local district court registry office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the certified corporate seal impression certificate from the registry, notarize the registry certification, and apply for Apostille (Hague states) or consular legalization (non-Hague states) through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the relevant embassy/consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative parallel mechanisms, not cumulative steps.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening must cover, at minimum, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, Korean Financial Intelligence Unit/KoFIU, Ministry of Economy and Finance, National Tax Service sanctions and tax evasion lists, INTERPOL and domestic law enforcement watchlists, adverse media, and global corporate registry disciplinary databases. PEP controls require risk-based identification of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their immediate family members, and close associates, verification using reliable public and commercial data, documented source of funds and source of wealth, escalation to senior management for high-risk relationships, ongoing transaction monitoring, and mandatory STR/SAR reporting to KoFIU under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO), with supplementary business license pre-clearance through the National Tax Service HomeTax and the StartBiz business-startup portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa name must be expressed in Hangul as the operating legal name; a foreign brand, including a Chinese-pastry trade name, must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul and may reflect a four-tier naming convention: (1) distinctive brand or creative element, (2) business-descriptive element such as bakery or pastry, (3) geographic or other permitted distinguishing element, and (4) the mandatory statutory suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. Chinese-character trade names may be recorded only as auxiliary references and never replace the registered Hangul name. The name must be sufficiently distinct from existing registered companies and must not mislead third parties as to its business character.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a rejection notice, counsel must request a written statement of the precise rejection ground from the registry officer. If the rejection rests on a conflicting identical or confusingly similar existing name, obtain an IRO extract of the prior name and either obtain the prior registrant's written coexistence consent under Commercial Act Article 23 or amend the Hangul transliteration with an additional distinctive element and refile. If the rejection rests on a prohibited or sensitive token, secure the competent authority's prior approval (for example, the Financial Services Commission for financial-word tokens or a food/bakery license for regulated food-sector words) and refile. If the registry still refuses, file an immediate appeal with the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within the same 14-day statutory window, attaching the written refusal, the amended Articles of Incorporation, and all supporting approvals. Failure to appeal within the deadline bars reinstatement, and a new name search will be required; the original 30-day reservation window will not be extended by internal registry review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered office for a licensed specialty bakery, master-franchise, and central-kitchen operation. The National Tax Service will deny or revoke a business registration certificate if there is no actual place of business in Korea, and the local licensing authority will not issue the required food-service or food-manufacturing license for a virtual mailing address. Banks also require an inspected physical operational address for account opening. A virtual office can only serve as an auxiliary correspondence address after a physical registered office, permitted retail store, and central kitchen have been properly leased, constructed, licensed, and registered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: (1) Food Sanitation Act license and pastry/bakery permits visibly posted; (2) production, refrigeration, warehousing, and sanitation equipment installed and functioning; (3) payroll-dependent employees present; (4) ingredient procurement invoices and batch records; (5) waste disposal contracts; (6) franchise disclosure and royalty documentation; (7) issuance of Korean electronic tax invoices from the registered premises. Risk quantification: approximately 70 percent likelihood of immediate inspection and enforcement action if the entity uses only a virtual office without any licensed physical location; approximately 35 percent likelihood during the first 12 months of operation after one central kitchen and one retail storefront are licensed; and approximately 15 percent likelihood in subsequent years if licensing, payroll, tax filing, and physical premises remain compliant.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and online registry search on the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory information and certificate issuance tariff; nominal per-search and per-extract fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of Articles of Incorporation required for Chusik Hoesa formation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Notary Public under the Notary Public Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on declared capital; approximate market range USD 300 to USD 800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court incorporation filing and registration tax on stated capital plus local education surtax
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korea Supreme Court Registry and the relevant municipal/local government
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Tax Act rate of 0.4 percent of stated capital for capital contribution registration, plus local education surtax and court filing fee; this estimate assumes approximately KRW 200 million stated capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal certification and certified corporate registration extract for the initial post-incorporation due-diligence pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official certificate fee schedule per certified copy

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National Tax Service business registration certificate and tax clearance certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official certificate fee, small actual issuance/copy fee; listed as nominal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter issuance by a Korean commercial bank after corporate account opening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean commercial bank issuing the reference
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff schedule for corporate reference/status letters; market range USD 50 to USD 200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of board resolution, power of attorney, seal certificate, and bank reference for outgoing foreign authentication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial per-document tariff; market range USD 150 to USD 400 for a consolidated bilingual document pack

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization processing fees for the six-document authentication bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, destination embassy/consulate, and authorized legalization service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official MOFA per-document fee, consular fee of the receiving mission, and market service-provider handling fee; per-document range USD 10 to USD 120

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean corporate counsel and cross-border due-diligence legal fee for Stage 1
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Korean law firm and international corporate counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customary fixed engagement fee for pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance, UBO/PEP screening, apostille/legalization workflow, and incorporation; market range USD 2,500 to USD 5,000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop, Act No. 1000, as amended), principally Articles 288, 289, 293, 295, 299, 302, 312, 317 and 319, together with the Registration of Non-Contentious Cases Procedure Rules and the Framework Act on the Registration of Real Estate, Corporations and Other Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office (Deunggi-so) of the Seoul Central District Court and local branch registration offices of the Court Administration Office, accessible via the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registry portal (iros.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Beobin Seollip Deunggi Sincheongseo), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, and organizational meeting minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa following the 2012 amendment to the Commercial Act. The promoters must resolve the issued capital amount, which must be fully paid in cash or lawful non-cash contribution to a designated bank account opened in the corporation's name before the incorporation registration. Withdrawal of contributed funds is prohibited until the company is effectively registered, except in the limited statutory cases of rescission or winding-up.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY_NAME] (Formal First Board Resolution). WHEREAS, [COMPANY_NAME] (the Company) was formed as a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and its promoters have completed the subscription and full payment of all authorized issued shares; and WHEREAS, the directors and statutory auditor duly elected at the organizational meeting have established a lawful quorum; IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: (1) the registered office of the Company is adopted at [registered office address in the Republic of Korea] for the custody of the corporate seal, statutory books, minutes, and share register; (2) the issued share capital of KRW [paid-in capital amount] divided into [number of issued shares] shares of common stock, fully subscribed and paid in, is ratified and recorded in the shareholders' ledger; (3) [representative director name] is appointed as the Company's representative executive officer (CEO) with exclusive authority to execute banking, franchise, lease, and licensing documents, while [finance officer name] is appointed as finance manager with joint signatory authority over banking matters; (4) [auditor name] is confirmed as statutory auditor; and (5) management is directed to file the incorporation registration, business registration, food sanitation permits, and all fire, structural, and occupational certifications without delay. This resolution is effective immediately. UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Administration Office electronic registration system (iros.go.kr) administered by the Supreme Court of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a pre-filing search of the corporate registry database to confirm that the proposed Chusik Hoesa name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing non-dissolved Korean corporation. File an online application for corporate name reservation. The same name cannot be used by another company, and foreign-language name equivalents are treated as identical names for this purpose. Reserve the legal name in Korean script for a period of up to four months.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation application form
Identification documents of each promoter or authorized agent
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
Statement of intended business purpose (bakery and central kitchen operation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the proposed name due to identity or similarity, file a written reconsideration request within three business days or resubmit the application with a modified and distinctive name. Rejection of the reservation does not affect later applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea and the Korean Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must execute and sign the Articles of Incorporation, specifying the corporate purpose (specialty bakery, Chinese pastry production, master franchise operation, central kitchen management, and wholesale distribution), the corporate name, the total authorized shares, the par value and class of shares, the location of the registered office, the method of public notice, the appointment of initial directors and statutory auditor, and the rules for general meetings and board meetings. The Articles must be notarized before a licensed notary public. Non-resident promoters may execute the Articles through a duly notarized and apostilled power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Promoters' identification or passport copies
Notarized power of attorney where applicable
Certified apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate or individual documents
Statement of in-kind contribution schedule, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires clarification or amendment, revise the Articles, initial each amended page, and re-execute before the notary. A notarial refusal may be cured by correction and resubmission, or by obtaining a written statement of the notary's reasons and applying for a court order approving the notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Shares and Deposit of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea; for in-kind contributions, the competent district court appointing an appraiser
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each promoter or subscriber must execute a share subscription statement. The entire issue price must be deposited into an account opened in the name of the corporation-to-be (not in the name of the promoters) at a commercial bank. The bank must issue a capital deposit certificate confirming the amount paid and the date of payment. If non-cash assets are contributed, a court-appointed examiner must appraise the contributed property at fair value, except for listed securities or property appraised by a certified public accountant under the Commercial Act. The deposit must remain frozen until incorporation registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Share subscription statements
Corporate bank account opening forms
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Appraisal report for in-kind contributions, if applicable
Proof of source of funds for anti-money laundering review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to documentation defects, resubmit corrected corporate identification and promoter documents. If the capital is underpaid, the parties must top up the deposit before the registration application; withdrawal or refund of contributed capital before registration is unlawful and is cured by restoration of the full amount plus statutory interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of the First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters' collective body; corporate officers to be recorded in the court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After full subscription and payment of the issue price, the promoters convene the organizational meeting to confirm the allotment of shares, elect the initial directors and statutory auditor for the statutory term, and inspect the performance of contributions. The newly elected directors convene the first board meeting and adopt the Formal First Board Resolution, which appoints the representative director (CEO), finance manager, and other officers, and fixes the registered office and banking signatory rules. Minutes of both the organizational meeting and the first board meeting must be executed and retained, and the officers' written acceptance of appointment must be obtained.
required_dossiers: Organizational meeting notice and minutes
First board meeting notice and minutes
Formal First Board Resolution
Written consents of directors, auditor, and representative director
Proof of capital contribution inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or auditor designated in the organizational meeting is disqualified or refuses office, convene an extraordinary organizational meeting and elect a substitute by majority vote. The resulting changes must be reflected in a supplemental minute and filed before the incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the competent district court (local Deunggi-so) and the Supreme Court electronic registry (iros.go.kr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after the expiration of the capital payment period, submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation to the registration office having jurisdiction over the registered office address. The application must attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, the organizational meeting and board minutes, the written acceptance of the directors, statutory auditor and representative director, and a specimen of the corporate seal. Pay the registration tax and local education surtax. The registration officer reviews compliance with the Commercial Act; upon approval, the registration is recorded and the company acquires separate legal personality. A certified copy of the corporate registration record will then be issued.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank-issued capital deposit certificate
Minutes of the organizational meeting and first board meeting
Written acceptances of directors, auditor, and representative director
Corporate seal specimen
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if any
Receipt of registration tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a request for correction, cure the identified defect within seven days by filing a supplementary document or amended application. If the registration is refused, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. Repeated rejection may be cured by re-filing with full compliance after correcting the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Registration and Activation of Corporate Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The competent National Tax Service district tax office for the corporate seal certificate; a licensed commercial bank for account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the issuance of the corporate registration record, register the corporate seal with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business. The tax office will verify the legal existence of the company and issue a Corporate Seal Certificate. In parallel, present the corporate registration record, the Corporate Seal Certificate, the First Board Resolution, and the representative director's identification to the bank where the initial capital account was opened, and lift the dormancy restriction to activate operational bank accounts and signatory authority for POS settlement and wire transfers.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the corporate registration record
Corporate seal certificate issued by the National Tax Service
Corporate seal specimen and seal impression card
Representative director's identification or passport
First Board Resolution appointing banking signatories
Corporate registration certificate for the bank's customer due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or bank challenges the identity of the representative director or the conformity of the seal, provide a notarized English translation of the corporate resolution and a certificate of the corporate seal recognized by the registration office. Any mismatch is cured by re-registering the seal and filing an amended board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Value-Added Tax Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (district tax office responsible for the principal place of business)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days from the incorporation registration, submit the Business Registration Application under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Select the appropriate business classification codes for food service activities, food manufacturing and processing, and wholesale trade, and list the head office and all planned store addresses that will operate POS terminals. Obtain the Business Registration Certificate and the unique business registration number. In parallel, file the payroll and social insurance registration with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service as an employer.
required_dossiers: Business registration application form
Certified copy of the corporate registration record
Lease agreement of the head office and store locations
Identification of the representative director
Corporate seal certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Food service or food manufacturing license, if already issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the application due to incorrect business classification or incomplete lease documentation, file an amended application with corrected codes and a supplementary lease affidavit. A tax office objection may be cured by administrative correction within seven days; further disputes follow the administrative appeal procedure under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Sanitation Approvals: Food Service Business Report and Food Manufacturing and Processing License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government (si/gun/gu) health and food safety department; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) where central kitchen approval is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For each franchised retail bakery cafe, submit the Food Service Business Report under Article 37 of the Food Sanitation Act and obtain the per-branch operating certificate before store opening. For the central kitchen that manufactures dough, pastry bases, and Chinese pastry finished goods, obtain a separate Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License from the competent local authority. Both filings require proof of compliance with the Food Sanitation Act facility standards, personnel hygiene requirements, HACCP obligations for applicable product categories, and verification of the store and kitchen blueprints, water supply, wastewater drainage, refrigeration, ventilation, and pest control plans. The license number must be displayed at the premises and printed on packaging.
required_dossiers: Food Service Business Report application form
Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License application form
Facility layout plans and equipment lists
Articles of Incorporation and corporate registration record
Business registration certificate and corporate seal
Food hygiene education certificates of the responsible managers
HACCP plan, if applicable to the central kitchen
Water quality inspection certificate, if a private water source is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority conditionally rejects or requires corrective measures, complete the remediation within the stated period and submit a written compliance confirmation. A formal denial may be appealed to the mayor or governor under the Administrative Procedures Act, and ultimately to the administrative court within ninety days of service of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Franchise Business Registration and Information Disclosure Statement Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fair Trade Commission of the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business model is a master franchise, the franchisor must prepare a Franchise Information Disclosure Statement compliant with the Fair Transactions in Franchise Business Act, including financial statements, franchise fees, royalty rates, territorial rights, supply obligations, and the trademark license scope. The disclosure statement must be filed and registered with the Fair Trade Commission before recruiting any franchisees. For international master franchise expansion, an English version may be prepared, but the Korean-language registered disclosure statement remains the governing operational document for Korean franchisees.
required_dossiers: Franchise Information Disclosure Statement (Korean version)
Certified financial statements of the franchisor
Articles of Incorporation and corporate registration record
Franchise agreement template
Food manufacturing and food service licenses
Trademark or service mark registration certificates
Royalty structure and fee schedule
List of current and planned franchisees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fair Trade Commission requires amendment of the disclosure statement, revise and resubmit within the specified correction period. Failure to register does not void franchise agreements but may subject the franchisor to administrative fines; the remedy is immediate compliance and supplementary registration of the corrected statement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), together with the local municipal government (si/gun/gu) food sanitation department and the Korea Food Safety Management Service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Service Business Report Certificate (eupso sildeung jeungmyeong) for each retail bakery cafe and Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License for the central kitchen and Chinese pastry production facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the Korea Environment Corporation (K-eco)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 4 - No mandatory Full EIA for operation of a bakery cafe or small-scale central kitchen; a Strategic Environmental Impact Registration may be required only where the facility footprint exceeds 10,000 square meters or the site falls within a protected watershed, greenbelt, or other environmentally sensitive zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from the central kitchen must be pretreated to meet the effluent quality standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act, including BOD no greater than 40 mg/L, COD no greater than 40 mg/L, total suspended solids no greater than 20 mg/L, and total nitrogen and phosphorus within applicable receiving-water standards. Baking oven exhaust and frying line emissions must comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Malodor Prevention Act, with odor dilution ratio at the property boundary not exceeding 15. Food waste, cooking oil, and sludge must be recycled or disposed through a licensed waste treatment contractor under the Waste Management Act and the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources, with manifests retained for at least five years.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.eia_registration_conditions: The facility must submit an environmental self-assessment and a waste management plan to the local environmental authority when commencing operation of the central kitchen. If the facility is located within a water-source protection area, a full Environmental Impact Assessment or prior permission from the Ministry of Environment is mandatory, and installation of oil and grease traps plus a real-time discharge monitoring connection to the municipal sewer system may be imposed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Inspection Certificate issued by the National Fire Agency and the local fire department under the Fire Services Act, confirming installation of fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency exits, and kitchen hood suppression systems; Building Completion Inspection and structural load verification under the Building Act, including a revised architectural record where heavy baking ovens and refrigeration units are installed; and an occupational safety and health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including a pre-commencement workplace risk assessment, machine guarding verification for dough mixers and sheeters, and a general safety inspection by the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA) for the central kitchen.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; digital portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa, the business registration number (BRN) issued by the National Tax Service constitutes the simultaneous corporate TIN and VAT registration number. The domestic legal representative must file an Application for Business Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office, within one month after corporate establishment, attaching the commercial registration certificate, articles of incorporation, board resolution appointing the representative, and passport/ID of the appointer. A foreign corporation operating in Korea without a Korean subsidiary must register its domestic place of business as a permanent establishment before beginning taxable activity, providing the foreign charter, proof of domestic office, and a Korean tax representative appointment where the foreign principal has no physical Korean presence. The NTS issues the BRN certificate immediately or generally within five business days, which is then used for VAT invoicing, customs clearance, and corporate income tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No entity classification check-the-box election exists under Korean law; a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxable as a corporation. Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation election for a domestic parent and its wholly or almost wholly owned Korean subsidiaries under the Corporate Tax Act; (ii) group filing elections for VAT on intra-group supplies where applicable; (iii) foreign tax credit versus deduction election for foreign-source income; and (iv) for cross-border hybrid mismatches, Korea applies mandatory BEPS Action 2 rules with targeted disallowance, not an elective regime. Taxpayers must disclose reportable international transactions under the Tax Adjustment on International Transactions Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to corporate entrepreneurs; any entity conducting taxable business supplies in Korea must register for VAT. The simplified taxpayer ceiling of KRW 80 million per annum applies only to certain individual entrepreneurs, not to Chusik Hoesa corporations. Foreign non-resident suppliers making Korean-source taxable supplies are also required to register regardless of amount, except where the reverse-charge self-assessment mechanism shifts the tax obligation to the Korean recipient.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices) apply to all entrepreneurs under the Korean VAT Act. Every VAT-taxable supply including bakery and franchise transactions must be documented by an e-tax invoice issued and transmitted to the National Tax Service through HomeTax, whether entered directly or via a certified ERP/API integration. The e-tax invoice must be issued on the supply date and transmitted to the NTS no later than the statutory VAT return filing deadline; in practice, NTS receives the invoice data electronically on or about the issuance date. Korea does not operate a Latin American-style real-time fiscal clearance stamp; instead, fiscal control is achieved through the HomeTax e-invoicing system, mandatory cash receipts for cash payments by individuals above KRW 100,000, and automatic reporting of card transaction data to the NTS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, zero-rating applies to exported goods and prescribed overseas services. For this bakery and Chinese pastry franchise, packaged food products manufactured in Korea and exported to foreign franchisees qualify for 0% VAT provided the goods are physically shipped out of Korea and supported by a customs export declaration. Franchise royalty fees and certain offshore service fees paid from abroad may also qualify as exported services when the place of supply is outside Korea and the service is actually rendered and consumed outside Korea, subject to Korean place-of-supply rules and transfer pricing documentation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service rigorously audits export zero-rating claims to prevent fictitious exports. If the exporter fails to produce valid customs, shipping, and foreign exchange substantiation, the zero-rated treatment is reversed and VAT at 10% is assessed on the supply. NTS may also levy penalty surcharges and late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act, and for deliberate fraud or false documentation, criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may lead to imprisonment up to five years and fines up to three times the evaded tax. Retroactive clawback extends to the statutory assessment period, which is lengthened in cases of intentional concealment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) jointly administer the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Bank of Korea acts as the central bank and the Foreign Exchange Information System is operated by the Korea Customs Service for reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is generally convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, service fees, royalties, and dividends, subject to reporting requirements under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment, loans, and acquisition of local financial products, are liberalized but require filing with a designated foreign exchange bank or the Korea Customs Service for statistical and supervisory purposes. Profit remittance by a foreign-invested company is permitted without prior approval if the entity has properly filed foreign investment reports and the remittance is supported by audited financial statements and tax clearance certificates. Practical hurdles may include documentary strictness, timing for verification, and requirements to convert foreign currency into KRW for local operational expenditures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 16 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related notices, export proceeds must be collected through a designated foreign exchange bank within a prescribed period; the standard statutory collection period is 180 days from the date of export declaration, extendable upon application. Mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW is not generally required for current account receipts, but export proceeds may be held in foreign currency accounts at domestic banks or overseas accounts pursuant to regulations. All export receipts must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System, and any settlement after the deadline requires a report with justification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) service providers have low direct viability in South Korea for primary corporate account holding due to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requiring the use of designated foreign exchange banks for cross-border settlements. Local fintech platforms like Toss and Kakao Pay may offer ancillary payments or operational accounts, but they are not substitutes for a corporate bank account at a licensed Korean bank. Use of offshore EMI for global treasury aggregation can be feasible for non-KRW, non-Korea cross-border collections, but for Korean operational settlements and regulatory compliance, a domestic designated foreign exchange bank is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korea's anti-money laundering regulations (under the Financial Action Task Force standards and the Financial Services Commission guidelines) require a physical presence or an in-person verification for foreign directors in most cases. A director can authorize a third party through a notarized power of attorney, but Korean banks generally require at least the beneficial owner or a senior manager to visit the branch in person for the initial onboarding interview. Remote opening is possible for certain non-resident individuals with an Alien Registration Card, but for a foreign corporate entity, remote onboarding is extremely rare and typically rejected. The recommended path is a physical visit by the foreign director or an authorized local representative to the designated bank branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign corporation with no local physical office and a single foreign director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Corporate Seal, Articles of Incorporation, beneficial ownership declaration, audited financial statements of the parent entity, business license, lease agreement or registered office address proof in Korea, and a notarized and apostilled Board Resolution appointing the authorized signatories and opening the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or layered corporate structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organizational chart until ultimate natural person shareholder, copies of IDs/passports of all beneficial owners holding 20% or more, source of wealth declarations, bank reference letters from the parent company's bank, and tax identification numbers in all relevant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of inbound cross-border intercompany payments without a clear commercial purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed master franchise agreement, royalty calculation schedule, VAT invoice, transfer pricing documentation, intercompany service agreements, and a treasury management policy document demonstrating the commercial substance of the flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive related party transactions in a bakery franchise network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed franchisee onboarding file, franchisee KYC documentation, sales reconciliation reports, POS system audit trail, inspection reports, and an explanation of the cash management and periodic deposit patterns.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injection must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank. The foreign investor must first file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remittance. The wire should use purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment' (e.g., reporting code 310000 or 320000 for equity). The receiving Korean company must issue a Foreign Investment Report Certificate before the remittance is received. The funds should be wired to a temporary foreign exchange bank account or the company's capital escrow account, and the bank will issue a certificate of acquisition of foreign exchange. Verification by the bank includes matching the remitter to the foreign investor, validating the foreign investment report, and confirming compliance with the minimum capital requirements for the intended limited liability company structure. The physical presence mandate and KYC interview for the foreign investor may be satisfied through the designated bank's Know Your Customer procedures for a non-resident investment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for raw material imports, equipment leases, and royalty payments are settled through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 messages via the designated foreign exchange bank. For import settlements, the payment must be supported by a valid import declaration, invoice, bill of lading, and the bank will report the payment under the Foreign Exchange Information System. For royalty and franchise fees, the payment is classified under service trade and requires a trade contract, tax invoice, and a withholding tax certificate issued after remote or withholding tax payment to the Korean tax authority. Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) can be used for high-value equipment imports or bulk raw material purchases, with the Korean bank acting as issuing bank. For recurring overseas vendor payments, the treasury should structure batches with a single purpose code and supporting contracts to streamline clearing and reduce compliance friction. Direct B2B local payments on the Korean Won rails (e.g., through the KRW payment and settlement system, BOK-Wire) are suitable for domestic supplier payables, but cross-border KRW payments are rare and generally discouraged; use USD or other major currencies for international wire legs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW forward contracts (plain vanilla) with a designated foreign exchange bank, available for real trade and service transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore or with approved Korean banks for KRW hedging, subject to the regulatory limits on speculative transactions and mandatory underlying documentation
Cross-currency swaps for intercompany loan interest and principal exchange, permitted when a genuine underlying transaction exists and reported to the central bank
FX options (plain vanilla call and put) on the KRW, permitted for hedging real exposures, but speculative positions are prohibited under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and tax settlement for the Chusik Hoesa, including tax adjustment schedules, financial statements, and supporting documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through Hometax, at the competent District Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a calendar-year fiscal year; extended to April 30 for corporations subject to external audit or filing through a licensed tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 20% of unpaid corporate tax for failure to file; 10% for understated or unfaithful filing; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% (capped at 75%); prolonged non-payment triggers compulsory collection and may result in a court dissolution order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate local income tax return and settlement (local income tax surcharge on corporate income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial / municipal tax office via Wetax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 for a calendar-year fiscal year; extension rules mirror the corporate income tax filing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 20% of local income tax; underreporting penalty of 10%; daily late-payment charges at the same rates applied to national corporate tax; asset seizure for continued non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and external auditor's report filed with the Financial Supervisory Service, if the entity meets the external audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART; also filed with the Securities and Futures Commission as required by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved at the annual shareholders' meeting by March 31 for a calendar-year fiscal year; audited report must be submitted to DART within two weeks after the external auditor's report date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 100 million for late or non-submission of auditor's report under the External Audit Act; may also invalidate corporate tax extension privileges and expose directors to liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise disclosure statement registration update for the bakery chain franchisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) through the franchise disclosure registration portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 120 days after fiscal year-end (April 30 for a calendar-year fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 100 million for failure to register or update the disclosure statement; prohibition on entering into new franchise agreements until registration is completed; corrective orders and increased franchisee rescission rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent external audit applies if total assets at the preceding fiscal year-end exceed KRW 5 billion (approximately USD 3.7 million); the entity is listed; or the company falls under one of the statutory categories in the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. A smaller Chusik Hoesa may also be audited on shareholder request if 1% or more of issued shares so demand.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS is mandatory for listed companies and applicable categories of unlisted corporations; unlisted private small and mid-sized companies may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for general-purpose financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a separate annual UBO declaration to the commercial registry. The Chusik Hoesa must keep its registered members list current at all times; each share transfer must be reflected in the registered members ledger immediately after transfer. For AML and banking purposes, ultimate beneficial ownership is re-confirmed on a rolling basis and must be identified in the annual franchise disclosure statement. The annual shareholders' meeting serves as the yearly point at which directors confirm the completeness of the register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and statutory auditors, if any)
Minute Book (shareholders' and board meeting minutes)
Corporate seal registration records and seal certificate documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,200 per year for licensed tax agent and office-address support; USD 1,500 – 3,000 per year for a prime commercial business address in central Seoul with secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 for a typical bakery franchise chain with annual revenue between USD 2 and 20 million; USD 12,000 – 30,000 for larger groups requiring consolidation or multiple-entity audit procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax (CIT) for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2023: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on taxable income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on taxable income from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion. An additional municipal local income tax surcharge is levied at 10% of the national CIT, producing aggregate statutory marginal rates of 9.9%, 20.9%, 23.1% and 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) may claim the small-enterprise income tax reduction under Article 7 of the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (a 5%–30% CIT reduction for 'small enterprises' with qualifying assets and revenue), R&D tax credits (up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure), job-creation and temporary investment tax credits, and reduced rates on income from new growth industries. For SMEs, net operating losses may be carried forward 15 years; non-SMEs are generally limited to a 10-year carryforward, and non-SME annual NOL deductions are capped at 80% of taxable income. A Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in bakery retail, franchise royalty receipt, and central kitchen manufacturing is taxed on worldwide income at the entity level; 100% non-resident ownership does not alter domestic corporate tax residence.
